challenge.method: Recomputed UTF-8 byte counts and SHA-256 for all nine full source bodies. Compared the publisher’s half-open byte range [0,1840) directly with the full standalone text and the JSON-decoded licenseText, preserving whitespace and line endings. Tested the full LICENSE and cutoffs one byte shorter and longer. Inspected the detail record’s lifecycle flag, alternate representations, and moving cross-reference. Checked the annotated tag name, release message, object identity, target type, and target SHA against the repository and commit in both SPDX data URLs.
challenge.results: Both SPDX representations matched all 1,840 bytes, with zero differences and shared SHA-256 a995449178fc587d652efb9a300d2db482a376c800ca3ce7346d8eeb613ba4dc. The 1,839-byte cutoff drops the final LF. The 1,841-byte cutoff adds an LF from the separator. The full-file comparison first diverges at byte offset 1840, where the SPDX text ends. The 1,553-byte publisher suffix begins with three additional LFs and introduces the tcpkill material. The Dug Song copyright begins at byte offset 1933. The detail record’s moving whole-file cross-reference reports match=false. Its template and HTML are distinct representations of 2,119 and 3,314 UTF-8 bytes. The annotated tag identifies v3.29.0 and points to the commit embedded in both SPDX data URLs. All nine full-body digests matched their capture envelopes.

limitations: Publisher scope is the captured LICENSE at the named ngrep commit. A mapping to a named ngrep release remains unestablished.
